exact_text:
A
breakout of an orderly channel is more likely to be the real thing than a
breakout of a high-volatility (disorderly) channel.
added_conditions: breakout of an orderly (low-volatility) channel is more likely to be genuine; disorderly (high-volatility) channels produce more false breakouts

exact_text:
you know that you have drawn your channel line correctly when a third relative high or low makes a touch of the line but doesn’t
cross it.
added_conditions: a channel line is validated when a third relative high or low touches the line but does not cross it

exact_text:
every time a price breaks a channel line, you face a
higher risk. The channel defines what is normal, and any foray outside the
channel is not normal.
added_conditions: on a channel-line breakout the three possible outcomes (new steeper channel, blowout breakout, or subsiding back into the channel) are unknowable from the chart alone; one may exit on every breakout or add another indicator

exact_text:
some
price bars will always break the channel lines without invalidating the
channel, unlike the situation in a hand-drawn channel.
added_conditions: in a linear regression channel some price bars always break the channel lines without invalidating the channel; widening the channel reduces mistaking a normal line break for a breakout

exact_text:
One technique for dealing with sideways moves within a channel is to draw
horizontal support and resistance lines off pivot points.
added_conditions: sideways action within a channel may warn that forward momentum is gone or imply an impending breakout in the opposite direction

exact_text:
So you start with the median
price and to that you add a factor to get upside resistance, and you subtract
a factor to get downside support.
added_conditions: a breakout a significant distance from the median price is needed to decide whether the old trend resumes or a reversal is at hand

added_parameters.name: R1 (first resistance)
added_parameters.value: pivot point value times two minus the low of the pivot day

exact_text:
trends are punctuated
by retracements, or small moves in the opposite direction before the trend
resumes.
a test of a previous high is commonplace in a bounce off a low.
added_conditions: target selection depends on risk appetite (R1 if risk averse, R2 if an optimist, R3 if aggressive)

exact_text:
he’s still willing to buy it for a short-term profit opportunity when a
momentum indicator says it’s temporarily oversold and likely to enjoy
a bounce upward.
added_conditions: only when a momentum indicator shows the price temporarily oversold

exact_text: This is a warning of an overbought or oversold condition and thus a potential retracement or reversal.
added_conditions: when the indicator approaches an extreme line of its recent range

added_parameters.name: oscillator extreme lines
added_parameters.value: 20 percent and 80 percent of maximum range (or 10 percent and 90 percent)

exact_text:
After a bounce up off a new low, traders hesitate to break it, but
after they do, the price accelerates to the next low.
added_conditions: historic highs and lows become benchmarks; after a bounce off a new low traders hesitate to break it, and once broken the price accelerates to the next low

exact_text:
you buy at the point where the price crosses
above the moving average line and sell at the point where it falls below the
moving average line.
added_conditions: trades are executed the next day at the open when working with daily data

exact_text:
When the shorter moving average crosses the longer moving average on the
upside, you buy. When the shorter moving average crosses the longer moving
average on the downside, you sell.

The more open space — daylight — you see between two moving averages,
the more confident you can be that the signal is correct and will continue.
added_conditions: when the two moving averages converge, confidence that the signal will last is lower

exact_text:
you
would consider a buy/sell signal to be confirmed only when both the 5-day
and the 10-day cross the 20-day moving average.
added_conditions: for buy-only traders, a sell signal occurs when the 5-day moving average crosses either of the other two moving averages

exact_text:
the crossover of the trigger and the MACD indicator occurs earlier than the crossover of the two moving averages in the top
window.

Technically, you don’t get a buy
signal until the bars are actually over the zero line
added_conditions: acting in anticipation of the zero-line crossover is optional

exact_text:
You sometimes get the
seeming paradox of a price reaching a new
high before the event and falling lower immediately after the event, even when the news
matches the forecast.
added_conditions: when the news matches the forecast, early birds take profit on the up move they engineered (sell on the news); if the news is much better than forecast, traders do not take profit and the price rises higher still

exact_text:
the RSI indicator tells you not to sell the
security short at this point, even though the price is still falling, because it is
about to reverse to an up move.
added_conditions: RSI going sideways near the 30 percent line while the price is still falling indicates an imminent reversal to an up move

exact_text: When %K crosses above %D, it’s a buy signal

a bearish
divergence is when the price is making a higher high but the stochastic forms a
lower high. The point is that momentum isn’t confirming the price action.
added_conditions: a bullish divergence is when the price makes a new low but the stochastic shows a higher low
